verdicts.why: Stays on 'taken advantage of', reads the word's force as the imposition felt from the sufferer's side, and its exclusivity claim holds against the family notes, none of which locates the wrong in the person's own feeling.

The vacancy is the word's own picture of the frivolity ('nothing inside to be serious with'), tied back to the gloss rather than drifting to a separate stupidity sense, and the contrast with dizzy matches dizzy's note.
Describes exactly 'thrown into a state of disarray' as a state the thing has been put into, stays inside the word, and its contrasts with broken and upset agree with those notes.
Locates the derision in the laugh the thing draws, which is the word's own construction, and the contrast with preposterous is the same one preposterous's note draws from the other side.

The gloss says 'repeated too often', so the overuse is already a fault, but the note says the wear is 'not held against the thing' and has 'smoothed it' — that is the worn-in, comfortable sense of well-worn (a path, a pair of shoes), not overfamiliarity through overuse.

Exclusive positional claim that collides with the family: 'the formal member of the group' claims the formal slot alone, but distressful in the same gloss group is noted as the stiffer, more formal shape of distressing, and the contrast offered against disturbing ('put out of its settled state' versus 'unseats it') draws no real difference.
Keeps to 'causing dejection' (the blue day that leaves one low), reads the word through its own colour metaphor, and its contrasts with dark and dismal match what those notes say of themselves.
